general.temas: Recurring stories cover the metro, weather forecasts, higher education and a solution to the pension system’s problems. Also featured are the condemnation of Iranian attacks on Bahrain and questions about Trump’s response to the US aviation crisis. Mada Masr stands out for its coverage of proceedings against journalists and the closure of the outlet itself.
general.motivo_crispacion: Much of the tension stems from attacks attributed to Iran against Bahrain, regional condemnations and Iranian threats. It is also generated by the war in Gaza and calls for aid, as well as disagreement between the parliamentary majority and the Egyptian opposition over military support for Saudi Arabia. Proceedings against journalists add to domestic tensions. These are offset by informational stories on transport, education, culture and sport.

Al-Masry Al-Youm.resumen:
- Two stories warn of heavy rain and strong winds as the Al-Maknesa storm arrives in Alexandria.
- The Ministry of Higher Education opens scholarship applications and highlights an initiative on youth responsibility; a school principal is reprimanded for charging improper fees.
- Reports cover cybersecurity training for ten countries and a meeting on water services in Fayoum. Police intervene at an unlicensed printing shop in Giza.
- A story questions Donald Trump’s silence over the US aviation crisis, citing The New York Times.
- The front page includes the launch of a lightweight version of PUBG Mobile, a concert in Jordan and a visual puzzle.
Al-Masry Al-Youm.motivo_populismo: Informational headlines predominate, although expressions such as “the most violent”, “if you have the eyes of a hawk” and the critical question about Trump add drama and sensationalism.
Al-Masry Al-Youm.sesgo: The selection gives space to institutional announcements and activities, alongside service news and entertainment. The headline about Trump takes a critical approach, suggesting that he prioritised the cinema over the aviation crisis.

Youm7.resumen:
- The Armed Forces welcome and honour outstanding athletes.
- The Transport Ministry announces cameras on trains and the metro; new trains and work on Line 4 are also highlighted.
- The Ministry of Higher Education is examining the implementation of 33,000 university appointments.
- Iran announces talks in Oman and Saudi Arabia condemns Iranian attacks on Bahrain; another headline questions Trump’s absence during an aviation crisis.
- The front page includes the weather forecast, information on car complaints and an official message of condolence.
Youm7.motivo_populismo: An informational tone predominates, although “Where is Trump?” uses a confrontational question and “the highest safety standards” adds a promotional emphasis.
Youm7.sesgo: The selection gives extensive visibility to authorities and public initiatives, particularly in transport, presenting their activities in a mostly favourable light. In international politics, it reports the Saudi condemnation and reproduces a journalistic criticism of Trump.

Akhbar El-Yom.resumen:
- The head of the social insurance authority says the pension system crisis will be resolved at the beginning of the new year.
- Several stories detail metro stations, excavation work and safety.
- Heritage features prominently, with reports on the Tahrir Museum and the first archaeological museum in the Middle East designed to exhibit antiquities.
- The front page covers the development of agriculture since 2014 and the opening of cultural theatres to students.
- It also reports an accident that injured 15 people, the date of a Zamalek match and the Arab Parliament’s condemnation of an Iranian attack on Bahrain.
Akhbar El-Yom.motivo_populismo: An informational tone predominates, although expressions such as “secrets of civilisation” and the description of the attack as “flagrant” add emotional emphasis.
Akhbar El-Yom.sesgo: The selection highlights infrastructure projects, heritage and cultural and institutional initiatives, taking a mainly descriptive approach. The agriculture story traces a shift from the loss of land to its recovery.

Al-Shorouk.resumen:
- The Revolutionary Guard announces the sinking of an oil tanker in the Strait of Hormuz; Iran threatens “many surprises”.
- Hamas calls for pressure to bring in aid and lift the blockade of Gaza; Rafah receives returning Palestinians and awaits patients and their companions.
- The dollar rises again and the head of social security expects the pension system crisis to be resolved at the beginning of 2027.
- One story examines the political weight of Arabs in Israel; another reports that two metro trains have entered service.
- Other prominent stories concern the historic trees at Cairo University and Youssef Ramadan’s swimming gold.
Al-Shorouk.motivo_populismo: An informational tone predominates, although the headline about Iran includes confrontational expressions such as “the enemy” and “its end is in our hands”, while the Hamas headline uses “occupation”.
Al-Shorouk.sesgo: The front page gives prominent attention to Gaza and regional tensions, alongside Egyptian economic and service issues. In its conflict coverage, it reproduces expressions used by the parties involved, though this does not mean the newspaper can be said to endorse them.

Mada Masr.resumen:
- The detention of journalists from “Matصدقش” is extended by 15 days; the headline denounces a lack of access and legal defence.
- Lina Attalah, editor-in-chief of Mada Masr, is detained after a fine of three million Egyptian pounds and an order to close the outlet. A challenge to two articles of the media law is also reported.
- A story examines damage to Palestinian olive groves and its effects on farmers.
- Parliament authorises the president to provide military support to Saudi Arabia; the opposition calls it a “blank cheque”. The detention of an Egyptian fishing boat in that country is also reported.
- Litigation over land in Saint Catherine is postponed and the final review of the IMF loan programme to Egypt begins.
Mada Masr.motivo_populismo: Informational headlines predominate, although expressions such as “no access, no defence” and “war on identity and resistance” add drama, and the opposition’s “blank cheque” criticism is highlighted.
Mada Masr.sesgo: The selection gives particular prominence to proceedings against journalists and takes a critical view of the conditions for their defence and restrictions on the media. In the story about Palestinian olive groves, the headline emphasises Palestinian identity and resistance.

opiniones.comunista:
Today I see a contradiction: new metro trains are entering service while a promise is made to resolve the pension system crisis at the beginning of 2027. For me, progress is measured not just by new machines, but by the material security of those who work and have worked. Cameras in the cabs are no substitute for investment in training and safe working conditions either.

I support public transport and pensions that are fairly funded and subject to democratic control by their workers and users. In the face of the power of big capital, collective ownership allows resources to be directed towards social needs, not private profit. And I am concerned about the closure of Mada Masr: without a free press, the working class loses tools for learning about the decisions that affect its life and holding those responsible to account.
opiniones.anarquista:
I am troubled that Mada Masr has been ordered to close and its editor-in-chief detained following a conviction for operating the outlet without a licence. A press that needs permission from those in power to exist can hardly hold them to account freely. Defending it does not require trust in any party: it requires journalists and readers to be able to organise and sustain independent reporting.

I also distrust the cameras announced for train and metro cabs. Safety matters, but making centralised surveillance of drivers the automatic response excludes those who know the job. I would prefer workers and users to participate directly in safety decisions, with transparency and without handing all authority to a control room. That is how collective freedom is built: by sharing responsibility, not accumulating power over others.
opiniones.liberal:
I am concerned about the closure of Mada Masr and the detention of its editor-in-chief following a conviction for operating a site without a licence. A free press should not depend on prior permission from the power it investigates. Defending freedom of expression also requires guarantees of a legal defence and independent courts, not just words.

The debate over hiring 33,000 people at universities raises another question: are all those positions necessary, and how much will they cost taxpayers? I want excellent universities, but I do not confuse more public-sector jobs with better results. Before expanding the state, I would demand clear accounts and room for private enterprise to compete and offer alternatives. Lower taxes give families room to decide; that freedom, in turn, requires personal responsibility and respect for the rights of others.
opiniones.extrema_derecha:
I see the parliamentary authorisation to provide military support to Saudi Arabia as a decision that demands scrutiny. Solidarity between nations cannot become a blank cheque: Egypt’s security, its soldiers and its sovereignty must come before commitments that political elites present as inevitable. I demand clear objectives and accountability.

I also support strict control of our borders. The Rafah crossing can accommodate patients and those returning to Gaza without Egypt giving up its right to decide who enters and under what conditions. Compassion is no substitute for the duty to protect our home.

Meanwhile, the heritage in our museums and the education of our young people deserve more than ceremonies. I want a state that preserves our traditions, guarantees reliable services and answers to citizens, not to the interests of the elites.
opiniones.centro:
I am concerned about the closure of Mada Masr and the detention of its editor-in-chief following the court ruling over the operation of a site without a licence. Rules must be obeyed, but they must also be open to challenge in court, and their penalties must be proportionate. An independent press and the right to a defence do not weaken institutions: they make it possible to correct their mistakes and deserve protection even when they are inconvenient for those in power.

I also see reasons to support the entry into service of new metro trains. Investment and cooperation with companies can improve everyday life, provided there is transparency and access for all. Likewise, I hope the announced commitment to resolving the pension system’s problems is fulfilled. I prefer gradual reforms whose results can be evaluated: an effective state, not one that asks for trust without being accountable.
